content: Most chickadees have **black beaks**. This is true for common North American species such as the Black-capped Chickadee (*Poecile atricapillus*), Carolina Chickadee (*Poecile carolinensis*), and Mountain Chickadee (*Poecile gambeli*). The beak is typically short, stout, and sharply pointed—well-adapted for their insectivorous and seed-eating habits—and consistently black in color across these species.
